title: Duke's remake of Koko and the definitive performance

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: There's an ironic little twist there, on that particular piece. I don't know if you heard a later recording that Duke did of that in 1956.
He had a different band and he redid some of those pieces. He played "Koko" again and it was--
Yeah, that may have been the only thing that went wrong, is that they had an off day.
Who knows about the quality of the A & R man at that time?
Yeah. But even when the guy who wrote the piece tries to do it over again, it may not work for various reasons.

No two performers are alike; thank God. There is no such thing as a definitive performer, there is only one that can isolate it per recording, or one that is allowed to grow. Before recording all we had was memory. We're talking about the way people listened in those days. You'd be exposed, maybe work alongside someone or work for someone who had a great influence on your thinking after that, but you went on with the memory of all this and built on it. It wasn't as though you could ever turn the tape on it and listen to it happen again, because what happened on that
tape was something of the moment; it had no real validity after that. You can use it just as you use a photograph. It's okay, but don't misrepresent with it.
